findings.title: Under Jenner only the CAS20 ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 and the three CAS20 singletons are routed to native code, and an address there with no token reverts every call, so no pool can hold funds in such a currency
findings.difference: From 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC (JennerTime 1796697000 in params/config.go line 256 at v1.8.2) BNB Smart Chain routes an address to native CAS20 code when bytes 0 and 1 are 0xCA52, bytes 2 to 9 are zero and byte 10 is 0x00 (Asset) or 0x01 (Stablecoin), and also routes the factory 0xCA5F00..00 and the registries 0x7020..01 and 0x7020..02. A token address whose code is not the one byte marker 0xEF reverts every call. Addresses in the same space with byte 10 from 0x02 to 0xff are ordinary accounts. The time precompile 0x70 answers any call with the block time in milliseconds. Ethereum has none of these. F-139 said every address in the CAS20 space reverts; that is true only for the two ordinals and the singletons.
findings.mechanism: core/vm/evm.go lines 46-59 (v1.8.2) first consults the static precompile map and, when IsJenner holds, calls resolveCAS20. resolveCAS20 (core/vm/cas20.go lines 122-135) returns the three singletons by exact address and otherwise, for an address that passes IsCAS20Address (bytes 2 to 9 zero, lines 50-60), looks up cas20Variants[addr[10]] (lines 107-119), which has entries only for 0x00 and 0x01. For any other ordinal the lookup returns ok = false and EVM.Call treats the address as an ordinary account (evm.go lines 318-360). For a routed token address runCAS20Token reverts unless the code hash equals keccak256(0xEF) (cas20.go lines 62-70 and 189-200; cas20_factory.go line 35). The cycle 19 probe that F-139 and lead L-907 rest on called 0xca52...0001, 0xca52...0000 and 0xca52...00ff, and all three have byte 10 equal to 0x00, so the reverts it saw for 'byte 10 = 0x02 or 0xff' were in fact ordinal 0x00 addresses. This cycle called byte 10 in {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0xff} on four endpoints with web3_clientVersion before and after each batch: ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 revert under the block time override 0x6b176e00 and ordinals 0x02 and 0xff return empty success, as the tag says, on Geth v1.8.2-4e1c8247 (dataseed and dataseed1), Geth v1.8.2-9b93ce23 and v1.8.2-132104cd (48 Club answered both builds in one batch) and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f on every cell it answered. For the PoolManager the effect is the one F-139 describes: for a routed address X with no token, take(X, to, 0) succeeds and moves nothing today and reverts after the fork (src/types/Currency.sol:64-86); sync(X) reverts before and after because the high level balanceOf call needs 32 bytes of return data (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). For an unrouted ordinal nothing changes at the fork: take succeeds and moves nothing, sync reverts. With no sync there is no settle credit (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so no delta, claim or liquidity in such an X can exist.
findings.impact: None. No pool can be funded in a CAS20 space currency that has no token, before or after the fork, and the fork changes nothing for the unrouted ordinals.
findings.preconditions: Jenner activates as scheduled. Token creation stays closed until a governance appointed administrator enables it (F-076). A token address can only become a token through the factory, because the marker code 0xEF cannot be deployed by CREATE or CREATE2 (EIP-3541) and bytes 0 to 9 fix 80 bits of the address.
findings.mitigations: None needed. The F-139 text should be narrowed to ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 and the three singletons.

sources.supports: IsCAS20Address checks bytes 0-1 = 0xCA52 and bytes 2-9 zero (lines 50-60); resolveCAS20Token indexes cas20Variants by byte 10 with entries only for 0x00 and 0x01 (lines 107-119); resolveCAS20 adds the three singletons (lines 122-135); runCAS20Token reverts unless the code hash is that of the marker (lines 62-70, 189-200); DisabledPrecompile makes dispatch treat the address as an ordinary account (lines 38-48)

EVM.precompile consults the map, returns not-a-precompile for DisabledPrecompile, and routes CAS20 only when IsJenner holds (lines 46-67); EVM.Call runs a precompile or the account's code (lines 299-360)
CAS20MarkerCode is the single byte 0xEF (line 35) and the factory writes it at token creation (lines 161-164)

sources.url: rpc: eth_call and eth_estimateGas from the PoolManager to CAS20 space addresses with byte 10 in {0x00,0x01,0x02,0xff}, singletons and 0x70, with and without blockOverrides time 0x6b176e00 and with and without a code override, on bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org, rpc-bsc.48.club and bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, 2026-11-25, research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-reserved-address-routing.work/raw/cas20_probe.json and raw/cas20_reth_retry.json
sources.supports: ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 and the singletons revert under the override, ordinals 0x02 and 0xff answer empty success with gas 21000, all four builds agree on every answered cell; publicnode refused part of the calls with a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403), recorded as refusals

cleared.check: L-907: which reading of CAS20 routing is right, the cycle 19 probe (byte 10 = 0x02 or 0xff reverts under Jenner) or the tagged source (only ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 are routed).
cleared.result: The tagged source is right and the probe was misread. The three cycle 19 addresses 0xca52...0001, 0xca52...0000 and 0xca52...00ff all have byte 10 equal to 0x00. A new probe with byte 10 in {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0xff} on dataseed1 (Geth v1.8.2 4e1c8247), dataseed (same build), 48 Club (two builds in one batch, 9b93ce23 and 132104cd) and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f, with web3_clientVersion before and after, shows ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 reverting and 0x02 and 0xff answering empty success with gas estimate 21000 under the Jenner time override, and all of them answering empty success without it. No build routes differently from the tag, so the lead's concern that validators on different builds disagree has no support in these answers.

cleared.check: L-908: every CAS20 function at v1.8.2 that changes a holder's balanceOf without a transfer signed or sent by that holder, who may call it, and whether an account with no role can move the PoolManager's balance between its own sync and settle.
cleared.result: No such path for an account with no role. balanceOf reads the raw balance slot for both variants (cas20_token.go lines 88-93); the Stablecoin variant adds only currency() (cas20_stablecoin.go lines 35-48); the Asset multiplier changes only scaledBalanceOf, balanceOfUI and totalSupplyUI (cas20_asset.go). The balance changing entries are mint and batchMint (MINT role, cas20_admin.go and cas20_asset.go lines 501-506), burn of the caller's own balance (BURN role), seizeWithMemo (SEIZE role, subject to the seize exempt policy), updateMultiplier (OPERATOR role, no balanceOf change), transferFrom (needs an allowance the PoolManager never grants; the PoolManager has no approve call) and permit (ecrecover only, cas20_permit.go lines 198-244, so a contract holder cannot be the signer). There is no interest, rebase, forced conversion or mint to all holders. A mint to the PoolManager between sync and settle credits the settler (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), but only a MINT role holder can do it, so it is an issuer action already recorded under F-007 and F-076.

cleared.check: L-887: whether a CAS20 token answers balanceOf or transfer differently when the caller is a contract under CALL, STATICCALL or DELEGATECALL.
cleared.result: Only the frame type matters, as the source says, and the PoolManager uses the frames that work. cas20EnterCall rejects DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE with DelegateCallNotAllowed() and any nonzero value with NonPayable() (cas20.go lines 88-100; DelegateCall passes directCall = false at evm.go line 461), and writes in a STATICCALL frame fail with write protection. On Chapel (Jenner active) the live token 0xca52000000000000000001217954ab5467577565, whose code is 0xef, was called from a contract placed by override: CALL balanceOf answered 32 bytes, STATICCALL balanceOf answered 32 bytes, STATICCALL transfer failed with 0xbeaba5b7, DELEGATECALL failed with 0x0d89438e, and CALL transfer(dead, 0) failed with PolicyForbids 0xa43fec12 because the token's sender policy does not list the caller, on Geth v1.8.1-56d84e62 (bsc-testnet.bnbchain.org) and on the cells reth-bsc answered. The PoolManager reads balanceOf with a high level view call, which compiles to STATICCALL (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96), and pays with CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:73), so neither the caller being a contract nor the frame changes what it sees.

cleared.check: L-917: on the five networks with protocol tokens or system code at reserved addresses, does an eth_call code override at such an address take effect, or does the node keep routing to native code.
cleared.result: It depends on the client and the range, and the answer is now measured. BNB Chain: the override takes effect at every CAS20 address, the singletons, 0x70, 0x1000 and 0x2000 on Geth v1.8.2 (override.go lines 75-82 put DisabledPrecompile in the map, and EVM.precompile then treats the address as an ordinary account, evm.go lines 46-51), and at CAS20 addresses on reth-bsc; reth-bsc keeps the native 0x70 precompile under Jenner and ignores the override there. Base: at the two live B20 tokens and at three unused 0xb200 + 9 zero byte addresses the stub is ignored; with any code present the native B20 code answers balanceOf with 0, while the same unused addresses without code revert. Tempo: the same holds for the 12 byte TIP-20 prefix (pathUSD and two live tokens answer natively, unused addresses revert with Uninitialized without code and answer 0 with code); the fee manager, TIP-403 registry, factory and DEX ignore the override. Arc: the override takes effect at 0x3600..0000, 0x3600..0001, 0x3600..0004 and 0x1800..0005 and 0x1800..0009. HyperEVM: the read precompiles 0x800 to 0x813 ignore the override; 0x2222..22, 0x3333..33, 0x5555..55 and the token system addresses 0x2000..00 and 0x2000..77 take it. On every reth or revm based endpoint (Ethereum, the OP Stack chains, Celo, X Layer, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM) and on avalanchego 1.15.3 an override at an active precompile (0x01, 0x02, 0x04, and 0x100 where active) is ignored, while Geth based bor, BSC and Nitro replace the precompile.

cleared.check: L-917 second half: which scripts and vectors in tools/opdiff and the work directories of cycles 9 to 19 placed a stand-in contract, the PoolManager build or a token double at an address in a reserved range, and which clearances rest on a call that tested neither the stand-in nor the real token.
cleared.result: None found. Every code override key in those scripts is a fresh address of the forms 0x..504d0001, 0x..d21fe00x, 0x..c0ffee0x, 0x..c0de0x, 0x..486b/486c0000 plus flags, 0x..beef or 0x..a11ce, or the network's real PoolManager address (pmdiff, pmdiff2, pmdiff6, callsem, statekeys, slotalias, stackedge, fwdgas, tcarry, tprobe). Scripts that touch reserved addresses (calleegas.py of cycle 13, edges.py of cycle 15, rb.py of cycle 16, tprobe.py of cycle 19, the cycle 19 CAS20 probe) call the real address without overriding its code. The sweep of this cycle shows that the PoolManager address of each network, the fresh pmdiff and battery addresses (20 addresses) and the sweeper itself answer as an ordinary cold account with no code (success, no return data, the network's cold access cost) or, for the PoolManager, run its own code and revert, on all 21 networks. So every earlier stand-in result tested the stand-in.

cleared.check: Task 4: on each network, which of 0x01 to 0x1ff, the PoolManager address and the pmdiff addresses are routed to native code, measured by a CALL with empty calldata and 200,000 gas from a contract placed by override (success, return size, gas used including access cost) against the same call on Ethereum.
cleared.result: The PoolManager address is routed to native code on no network: on all 21 it runs code and reverts with no data at the cold access cost plus about 50 gas (Monad: its 10,100 cold access plus 42). The pmdiff addresses are ordinary everywhere. Addresses in 0x01 to 0x1ff that answer as something other than a cold empty account: 1: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 10: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 8453: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 130: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 7777777: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 480: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 57073: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 1868: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 42220: 0x1-0x11 0xfd 0x100; 196: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 42161: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x6b-0x74 0xc8 0xff-0x100; 4663: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x6b-0x74 0xff-0x100; 99901: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x6b-0x74 0xff-0x100; 137: 0x1-0x9 0xb-0x11 0x100; 56: 0x1-0x11 0x64-0x69 0x70 0x100; 43114: 0x1-0xa 0x100; 143: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 4326: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 4217: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 5042: 0x1-0x11 0x100; 999: 0x1-0xa. Ethereum routes 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x100. Differences from Ethereum inside those sets are in precompile pricing or presence (Polygon 0x06 to 0x08 and no 0x0a, Avalanche and HyperEVM without 0x0b to 0x11, HyperEVM without 0x100, Monad and MegaETH pricing, Monad 0x08 failing on empty input) and in chain specific precompiles (Arbitrum family 0x64 to 0x74, 0xc8 and 0xff, BNB Chain 0x64 to 0x69 and 0x70, Celo 0xfd). None of this changes what src computes: the only external call sites are Currency.sol:48 (native payout to a caller named address), Currency.sol:73 (transfer on a caller named currency), Currency.sol:94 (balanceOf on a caller named currency), Hooks.sol:134 (the pool's hook) and the unlock callback to msg.sender, so the PoolManager reaches a precompile only when a caller names one, and earlier cycles swept those addresses under P1, P2, P3 and P5 with no credit found.

cleared.check: Whether an ordinary account can make an unused address in a native token range look like a token (B20 and TIP-20 treat any code as an initialized token; CAS20 needs the marker 0xEF), and so open or close a currency that pools could use.
cleared.result: No. Base routes 0xb2 followed by 9 zero bytes (flipping byte 9 or any earlier byte gives an ordinary account, flipping byte 10 or later stays routed), Tempo routes the documented 12 byte prefix 0x20c0 + 10 zero bytes, and CAS20 fixes 10 bytes. Getting code at such an address needs a CREATE or CREATE2 address or a private key with 80 to 96 fixed bits, and the CAS20 marker 0xEF cannot be deployed at all (EIP-3541). Tokens are created only through each network's factory. A pool whose currency is such a token is a pool with an issuer, already covered by F-027, F-031 and F-076.

leads.question: Should tools/opdiff refuse a state override whose address is an active precompile or a native token range on the target network (reth and revm based endpoints and avalanchego ignore it, Base and Tempo keep native token code and treat the override as an initialized token)?
leads.why: No earlier script placed a stand-in there, but a future harness that does would compare native code with the reference and could clear a path it never ran.

leads.question: Monad's 0x08 (BN254 pairing) fails and consumes all forwarded gas on empty input, where the specification and Ethereum return 1; is that the consensus behaviour of Monad 0.16.7 or an RPC artefact?
leads.why: src never calls 0x08 and 0x08 is not a valid hook address, so there is no PoolManager impact; it is a precompile divergence that the opcode battery does not cover.

leadResults.answer: The cycle 19 addresses all had byte 10 = 0x00; the tag is right. Ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 and the three singletons are routed under Jenner and revert without a token; ordinals 0x02 and 0xff are ordinary accounts, on Geth v1.8.2-4e1c8247, -9b93ce23, -132104cd and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f. F-139 is restated accordingly.

No CAS20 function lets an account without a role change another holder's balanceOf; every such change needs the MINT, BURN (own balance only) or SEIZE role, an allowance or an ecrecover permit. The Stablecoin variant adds only currency().

On Chapel a live token answers balanceOf under CALL and STATICCALL from a contract, refuses DELEGATECALL with DelegateCallNotAllowed and STATICCALL writes with write protection, as the v1.8.2 source says. The PoolManager uses STATICCALL for balanceOf and CALL for transfer.

Measured on all five networks and on all 21 for precompiles: BSC Geth and Arc honour code overrides at reserved addresses, Base B20 and Tempo TIP-20 keep native token code, reth and revm based clients and avalanchego keep active precompiles, HyperEVM keeps 0x800 to 0x813. No earlier script placed a stand-in in any of these ranges, so no clearance rests on an untested stand-in.
